thematic_title: The Pattern Parade — Growing, Shrinking, and Numbers to 100
descriptive_title: Grade 2 Mathematics: Algebra (Patterns and Relationships) — Repeating, Growing, and Shrinking Patterns with Tables of Values and Whole Numbers up to 100 (C1.1–C1.4)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Grade 2 unit on Algebra (C1.1–C1.4), framed as a parade led by Coco the Conductor and four Canadian animals. Children identify repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns; name rules in +N or -N notation; build tables of values; predict faraway terms; and lead a number parade up to 100.
long_description:
Take patterns from Grade 1 noticing into Grade 2 reasoning. The Pattern Parade — Grade 2 Edition is a 5-day, ready-to-teach unit that takes children on a journey with Coco the Conductor and the Parade Animals — Bea the Bear, Finn the Fox, Bibi the Beaver, and Moss the Moose — to identify repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns, name rules using +N / -N notation, translate one pattern across animal parade, number sequence, AND table of values, justify their predictions for faraway terms (term 10, term 20), and finally build repeating number parades using whole numbers up to 100.

Each lesson is fully scripted with teacher prompts, structured for active and partner-rich learning, and includes a printable student worksheet that consolidates the day's thinking. Children build animal parades with manipulatives, name their rules using +N or -N notation, organize their thinking into tables of values (the Grade 2 representation), predict faraway terms WITHOUT drawing every step, and finally lead their own number parade as Junior Pattern Conductors.

What makes this unit different:
- Aligned to all four Ontario Grade 2 Algebra expectations (C1.1, C1.2, C1.3, C1.4) — no gaps, no drift.
- A single coherent narrative across 5 days: recurring characters, threaded vocabulary (term, growing, shrinking, +N rule, table of values, justify), an anchor chart that grows day by day.
- Four-track differentiation built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners.
- Detailed teacher scripts for the conceptually trickiest moments — Lesson 3 (table of values, the keystone) and Lesson 5 (animals to numbers up to 100) — including expected misconceptions and recovery moves.
- Real-life pattern hunt in Lesson 1 with Canadian classroom contexts (calendar, hopscotch, brick walls, snowflakes).
- A standalone mid-unit formative ('The Three Pattern Types Check') administered between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4 as a 12-minute gate before the unit's hardest content.
- Manipulatives ready to print (default black and white so any classroom printer works), plus reusable assessment trackers per lesson.
- Student-friendly Junior Pattern Conductor certificate for the closing ceremony.

Designed for Canadian classrooms: Canadian animals, the spelling 'colour' throughout, references to familiar Canadian community parades and schoolyard contexts, and Ontario Grade 2 conventions for assessment. The recurring cast (Coco + Bea, Finn, Bibi, Moss) is visually identical to the Kindergarten and Grade 1 Pattern Parade units, so a child returning from earlier grades recognizes the characters immediately.

Total classroom time: about 255 minutes across 5 lessons. Teacher prep time: about 110 minutes one-time, then the printables are reusable next year. Suitable for any Grade 2 teacher in Ontario introducing growing/shrinking patterns and number patterns up to 100, or any teacher building from a Grade 1 patterns base into the Grade 2 expectations.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans (50–55 minutes each, ~255 minutes total of teaching time)

4 class observation trackers: 1 diagnostic (Lesson 1) plus 3 formative (Lessons 2, 3, 4) — each with grade-2-specific column headers including +N notation, table of values, and far prediction
1 four-level summative rubric covering all four expectations (C1.1–C1.4) with Grade 2 descriptors aligned to the 0-100 number range and table-of-values representation
1 summative administration guide tying the worksheet, lesson, and rubric together for the teacher
Junior Pattern Conductor certificate (one per child) for the closing ceremony
Detailed expanded walkthroughs for Lesson 3 (the keystone — table of values reveal) and Lesson 5 (animals to numbers up to 100), including expected student misconceptions and teacher recovery moves
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners
Real-life pattern hunt (Lesson 1) with Canadian classroom contexts — calendar, hopscotch, brick walls, snowflakes
target_buyer: Grade 2 teachers in Ontario, or any teacher building from a Grade 1 pattern base into Grade 2 algebra expectations. Especially valuable for teachers who want a coherent multi-day unit that progresses from identifying the three pattern types to naming rules in +N notation, organizing patterns into tables of values, predicting faraway terms, and translating into number patterns up to 100.
subject: Mathematics
pedagogical_approach: Active, oral-first, movement-rich, with a Grade 2 emphasis on naming rules in formal +N / -N notation, organizing patterns into tables of values, and predicting faraway terms WITHOUT drawing every step. Worksheets are end-of-lesson consolidation, never the main activity. Student-generated patterns are honoured — children who invent unusual rules (e.g., +5 -2 alternating) are celebrated and documented for the receiving Grade 3 teacher. Assessment uses a 4-level rubric across each expectation paired with anecdotal observation notes. Number patterns up to 100 (C1.4) are scaffolded by reusing the same rule notation children practiced with animals all week — the rule does the cognitive work, the larger numbers add the new layer.
